rules.description: Tool input and output schemas must be valid under their applicable JSON Schema dialect. Unsupported declared dialects are errors; unresolved external references warn when complete offline checking is unavailable. External schemas are not fetched automatically, and a partial check is not reported as complete.
rules.notes: The declared dialect set is fixed by the specification, not by the validator: an unsupported dialect is an error, not a warning, because MCP guarantees only 2020-12 support and peers return an error for other dialects, and because Tool examples cannot be checked against a schema in an unknown dialect (maintainer decision on issue #72, 2026-10-26). Unresolved external references differ: offline validation forbids retrieving them, so they only warn. Earlier revisions define no embedded dialect; mcp.tool.schema.legacy-shape applies there instead.

rules.summary: When a Tool declares outputSchema, a successful result contains structuredContent.
rules.title: Supply structured content when an output schema needs it

rules.description: Legacy HTTP plus SSE remains representable but is deprecated for later MCP protocol versions. The warning does not by itself invalidate the document. Review whether the server still offers that transport or whether the description should advertise Streamable HTTP instead.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-03-26 specification, Basic, Transports, Backwards Compatibility (deprecated HTTP+SSE transport)

rules.summary: Legacy HTTP+SSE associated with MCP 2025-03-26 or later is reported, because Streamable HTTP replaces it.
rules.title: Review deprecated legacy SSE transports

rules.description: Streamable HTTP is not defined by the earliest supported MCP protocol version. Scope the transport to versions that define it and keep root protocol coverage consistent. A URL alone does not make a transport applicable to every protocol version.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-03-26 specification, Basic, Transports, Streamable HTTP (replaces HTTP+SSE from 2024-11-05)

rules.summary: Streamable HTTP is used only from MCP 2025-03-26.
rules.title: Use Streamable HTTP only where supported

rules.description: A completion example must target a Prompt argument or Resource Template variable that exists. Context entries must name other declared targets, not repeat the argument being completed. Correct the example names or the declaration they describe.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-06-18 to 2026-07-28 schema.ts, CompleteRequest context.arguments (previously-resolved variables in a URI template or prompt)

rules.summary: A completion example completes a declared Prompt argument or URI template variable, and its context names other declared arguments or variables only.
rules.title: Complete a declared argument or template variable

rules.description: A component reference must identify an existing value in the namespace required by its use site, without a reference cycle. Check both the target name and the namespace. Reuse does not exempt the resolved value from validation in its containing declaration.
rules.summary: A Reference Object targets an existing component in the namespace its use site requires, without cycles.
rules.title: Resolve component references in the right namespace

rules.description: The structural schema checks required fields, types, allowed members, and collection shapes. Use the diagnostic path to locate the invalid value. Passing this check is necessary but does not replace semantic checks such as reference resolution or protocol scoping.
rules.summary: A document validates against the JSON Schema for its declared mcpdesc version. Used for structural failures not attributed to a more specific rule.
rules.title: Match the MCP Description document schema

rules.description: Form properties, required names, enum labels, defaults, and bounds must agree with one another. Correct references to absent properties and contradictory constraints. Passing JSON Schema's outer shape checks does not prove that the declared form is internally consistent.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-06-18 to 2026-07-28 schema.ts, PrimitiveSchemaDefinition and EnumSchema (enumNames are display names for enum values)

rules.summary: A form requestedSchema is internally consistent: required names declared properties, enumNames match enum values, defaults lie within enums, and minimum bounds do not exceed maximum bounds.
rules.title: Keep elicitation form constraints consistent

rules.description: Elicitation declaration names identify interactions within their primitive. Duplicate names make a Tool interaction's declaration reference ambiguous. Rename one declaration and update the references that are intended to select it.
rules.summary: Elicitation Declaration names are unique within their primitive.
rules.title: Give each elicitation declaration a unique name

rules.description: An example result is the completed payload, not a JSON-RPC response or a pending workflow. Remove envelope fields such as jsonrpc and id and do not include task or input-required state. Multi-step interactions belong in the explicit interaction example structure.
rules.notes: Envelope fields are jsonrpc, id, and error. Non-completed workflow fields are task, inputRequests, and requestState. They are excluded from the field classification of mcp.result.additional-properties.preserve.

sources.reference: MCP 2026-07-28 schema.ts, InputRequiredResult (inputRequests, requestState) and Result.resultType
MCP 2025-11-25 schema.ts, CreateTaskResult (task)

rules.summary: An example result is a completed result payload: it contains no JSON-RPC envelope field and no non-completed workflow field.
rules.title: Show completed results without message envelopes

rules.description: A completed example result must contain the fields each applicable MCP protocol version requires, with valid values. Check the result's full effective scope, not only the newest version. Fields permitted but undefined on open result types are handled separately as warnings.
rules.notes: Fields a revision does not define are governed by mcp.result.additional-properties.preserve (accepted with a warning). When present, resultType must be "complete", ttlMs non-negative, and cacheScope "public" or "private" in every revision (document schema).

sources.reference: MCP 2026-07-28 schema.ts, interface Result (resultType required) and interface CacheableResult (ttlMs, cacheScope required)

specification.reference: Examples fail fast decision (validation README, 2026-10-25, issue #72)

rules.summary: An example result contains every field that each applicable MCP revision requires, and every field a revision defines has a valid value.
rules.title: Match example results to every applicable version

rules.description: Extension identifiers in an MCP-reserved namespace are checked against the pinned catalogue. Unknown or experimental identifiers are preserved with a warning. Verify the identifier and its maturity; an unrecognized identifier is not silently assigned known extension semantics.
rules.notes: The pinned catalogue lists no experimental identifiers, so no document currently produces the experimental-identifier warning.

sources.reference: MCP 2026-07-28 specification, Basic, General fields, _meta key name format (second label modelcontextprotocol or mcp is reserved)

specification.reference: MCP Description 0.9.0, Sections 8.4 and 8.5; validator extension catalogue (effective 2026-09-04)

rules.summary: An extension identifier under an MCP-reserved prefix that the pinned extension catalogue lists as experimental, or does not list, is preserved with a warning.
rules.title: Review reserved extension identifiers

rules.description: MCP 2024-11-05 and 2025-03-26 receive structural and selected checks, not a claim of complete MCP semantic conformance. The warning describes a validation limitation rather than an invalid document. Adding a later protocol version does not make checks for the earlier versions complete.

specification.reference: MCP Description 0.9.0, Sections 3.5 and 16.2; Proposal 0024, Section 4.1 (revision tiers)

rules.summary: A document applying to MCP 2024-11-05 or 2025-03-26 is reported as receiving structural and selected checks only, not complete MCP semantic conformance.
rules.title: Limited validation for early MCP protocol versions

rules.description: Native projection selects a Tool, Resource, Resource Template, or Prompt by its identifier in one protocol view. A declaration outside that view cannot be projected for that version. Check the identifier and the declaration's inherited or explicit scope.
rules.notes: Implemented by @mcpdesc/core; this repository checks the fixtures with scripts/test-projection-fixtures.mjs.
rules.summary: Native projection selects one declaration of the requested kind and identifier in the Effective Protocol View of the revision.
rules.title: Select an applicable declaration for projection

rules.description: Native projection resolves Tool schema components, removes description-only fields, and checks the value against the selected MCP schema. It does not repair values or invent defaults. A postcondition failure is an implementation or specification defect and returns no projected value.

gaps.behavior: A valid document can give a Tool schema property a boolean subschema, which JSON Schema 2020-12 allows, while the pinned MCP 2025-11-25 schema.json requires an object there. Projecting that Tool for MCP 2025-11-25 fails the postcondition; MCP 2026-07-28 accepts it.

rules.notes: The postcondition cases come from the recorded gap, not from an injected fault: the source is valid, yet the native value fails the pinned MCP 2025-11-25 schema. A list fails as a whole. scripts/test-projection-fixtures.mjs checks that each failure case's value really fails that schema and that every expected value passes it.

specification.reference: MCP Description 0.9.0, Section 4.14, steps 4 to 6, no synthesis, and lists

rules.summary: A native projection keeps exactly the declaration fields that the MCP type defines in the revision, unchanged after reference resolution, and the value validates against the pinned MCP schema of the revision.
rules.title: Preserve MCP values when projecting declarations

rules.description: Native projection first validates the source and checks that the requested MCP protocol version appears at the root. Fix source errors or select a declared version. These failures come from the projection operation, not a new document-validation phase.
rules.notes: Implemented by @mcpdesc/core; this repository checks the fixtures with scripts/test-projection-fixtures.mjs.
rules.summary: Native projection starts from a document without validation errors and from a revision in its root protocolVersions.
rules.title: Project a valid source and declared protocol version

rules.description: A Prompt example supplies every required argument and no undeclared argument. Check names against the containing Prompt, including when the example comes from a reusable component. Omitted optional arguments do not need placeholder values.

sources.reference: MCP 2024-11-05 to 2026-07-28 schema.ts, interface PromptArgument, required ("Whether this argument must be provided")

rules.summary: A Prompt example supplies every required Prompt argument and no undeclared argument.
rules.title: Supply the Prompt arguments the example requires

rules.description: An omitted scope inherits its parent's full scope; an explicit child scope must stay within it. Declarations with the same identity cannot overlap where the specification requires uniqueness. Narrow the scopes rather than expecting the validator to choose one variant.
rules.summary: Nested protocol scopes stay within their parent scope, and same-named primitives and capability objects do not overlap in protocol scope.
rules.title: Keep protocol scopes consistent and disjoint

rules.description: A Resource Template example records the concrete requested URI, which must be an RFC 6570 expansion of the containing template. Check the template and URI together, including examples reached through components. Matching a URI does not require network retrieval.

sources.reference: RFC 6570, URI Template

rules.summary: A Resource Template example uri is a valid RFC 6570 expansion of the template.
rules.title: Use a concrete URI that expands the template

rules.description: Resource example contents are compared with the declaration's requested URI, MIME type, and declared raw size. A mutable resource can differ between observations, so size differences are warnings. Review the example and declaration together rather than inferring live content.
rules.notes: Collections and indirect reads may legitimately differ, so these are warnings.
rules.summary: Resource example contents agree with their declaration: the requested URI is returned, MIME types match, and raw size matches a declared size.
rules.title: Keep Resource examples consistent with declarations

rules.description: Security requirements refer to named schemes, and scopes have meaning only for OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect schemes. Correct missing references or repeated scopes. An uncatalogued scope can produce a warning where the scheme declares a static scope catalogue.
rules.notes: The document schema rejects duplicate scopes first; the semantic duplicate-scope check applies only to direct callers of the semantic validator.
rules.summary: Security requirements name declared schemes, list scopes only for OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect schemes, do not repeat scopes, and use catalogued scopes when the scheme declares a static catalogue.
rules.title: Reference security schemes and scopes correctly

rules.description: When the document declares a tag catalogue, primitive tag references must name entries in it. Root tag names and repeated primitive references are checked for duplicates. Fix the name or catalogue entry instead of relying on an undeclared alias.
rules.summary: Root tag names are unique, and primitives reference only declared tags.
rules.title: Reference unique declared tags

rules.description: Tool execution errors are completed MCP Tool results with isError true, not a separate description-only error catalogue. Check the error result's content and avoid presenting successful structured output as the error payload.
rules.notes: MCP does not forbid structuredContent on error results; MCP Description requires its absence so that example structuredContent always conforms to outputSchema.

specification.reference: MCP Description 0.9.0, Section 9.3 (an execution-error result MUST NOT contain structuredContent; outputSchema does not validate error content)

rules.summary: A Tool execution-error example result sets isError to true and does not contain structuredContent.
rules.title: Represent Tool execution errors as error results

rules.description: Example input must satisfy the resolved inputSchema, and successful structured output must satisfy outputSchema when supplied. Correct the example or the declaration's schema. Where resolution or dialect support prevents complete checking, the diagnostic must make that limitation visible.
rules.notes: Before MCP 2025-11-25 no embedded dialect is defined, so only the legacy shape is checked and the warning reports the gap.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-06-18 to 2026-07-28 specification, Server Features, Tools, Output Schema (structured results conform to outputSchema)

rules.summary: A Tool example input validates against inputSchema, and its structuredContent against outputSchema, for every applicable revision; incomplete validation is reported.
rules.title: Check Tool examples against their schemas

rules.description: A Tool interaction example can contradict its explicit minimum client requirements. Review the warning against the scenario and the declared requirements. The example does not automatically create or strengthen a client requirement.
rules.notes: Steps never create requirements; the warning reports a contradiction only.
rules.summary: Interaction steps do not contradict the Tool's explicit client capability requirements.
rules.title: Keep interactions consistent with client requirements

rules.description: A Tool's elicitation step must agree with the named elicitation declaration and its requested form. Accepted form content must satisfy that schema, while declined or cancelled responses have different content rules. Check the reference, request, and response together.

sources.reference: MCP 2025-06-18 to 2026-07-28 schema.ts, interface ElicitResult, content (present for accepted form responses)

rules.summary: An elicitation step matches the Tool's named Elicitation Declaration, and its response content is present exactly when an accepted form response requires it and validates against the requested schema.
rules.title: Match elicitation steps to their declaration

rules.description: When transports are declared, every root protocol version must be covered by at least one transport's effective scope. An omitted transport scope inherits all root versions. Add appropriate coverage or narrow the documented protocol versions rather than leaving an unreachable view. Descriptions may omit transports entirely.
rules.summary: Every protocol version at the root is covered by at least one transport when transports are declared.
rules.title: Cover each declared protocol version with a transport
